metadata.title: Crypto Exchange Gemini Offers Zero-Commission Stock Trading

content.text:
Crypto exchange Gemini (NASDAQ: $GEMI) is offering zero-commission stock trading in the U.S. as it looks to grow into an all-in-one financial app.
Gemini, which is run by twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, is now offering 0% commission on stock trading in most U.S. states.
"We started with crypto and are expanding to stocks so that customers can manage their entire financial lives right from the Gemini app, said President Cameron Winklevoss in a news release.
More From Cryptoprowl:

Eightco Secures $125 Million Investment From Bitmine And ARK Invest, Shares Surge
-
Stanley Druckenmiller Says Stablecoins Could Reshape Global Finance
Zero-commission stock trading has become the industry standard in the U.S. following the success of fee-free brokers such as Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: $HOOD).
The move also comes a crypto exchanges such as Gemini look to expand their offerings beyond Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) to stocks, bonds, and commodities trading.
Gemini said in its news release that it is looking to become an "all-in-one financial super app."
Zero-commission brokers typically find other ways to make money, such as through payment for order flow, interest on uninvested cash, margin lending, and premium subscriptions.
"Crypto was just the beginning. Our goal is to bring many financial products, from crypto to equities to derivatives, under one regulated platform," said Tyler Winklevoss, Gemini's CEO.
Gemini was founded in 2014 and went public last September. Since then, GEMI stock has declined 87% to trade at $4.22 U.S. per share.
